The poll found that 35% of Americans approved of the president's job performance, up two percentage points from the previous Reuters/Ipsos tracking poll released in early September. Trump’s slight improvement in the newest poll came after three straight weeks of the lowest approval numbers he had seen in Reuters/Ipsos tracking since his return to the White House in 2025. results.content: Trump’s approval and economic ratings point to a gloomy environment for the GOP, but the race for Congress is closer than in his first midterm, with the Democratic Party still unpopular. The president’s approval rating stands at 41% among registered voters, a second-term low in the poll, with a majority (55%) of voters saying they believe Trump’s policies have hurt the economy. Democrats hold a 5-point edge in the battle for control of Congress, 50%-45% — not nearly as large a lead as the 12-point advantage the party enjoyed at this point before the 2018 election, when Democrats rode an anti-Trump wave to the House majority in his first midterm as president. # Diesel prices hit new record in September 2026: What that means for inflation, shipping costs and your portfolio

September 15, 2026

Diesel prices hit record highs in early September, rising faster than gas. Here's what surging diesel costs mean for inflation, shipping and your investment portfolio – and what to watch next. [...] Here’s a practical checklist for investors to consider:

   Revisit diversification and check for concentrated exposure to transport-intensive or margin-sensitive areas.
   Stress-test your financial plan. How would it hold up if inflation stays firmer for longer (compared to a temporary fuel spike)?
   Focus on goals and time horizons, not short-term moves.
